cards.back: To succeed in reaching a particular goal or result through effort. "She worked hard to achieve her target score on the exam." Common collocations: achieve a goal, achieve success, achieve results.

A condition or factor that puts someone in a favorable position. "Living near the university gives students a clear advantage." Common collocations: take advantage of, have an advantage, competitive advantage.
To have an influence on or cause a change in something. "The weather can seriously affect people's mood and energy levels." Common collocations: deeply affect, directly affect, adversely affect.

A way of dealing with a situation or problem; to come near. "The team adopted a new approach to solving customer complaints." Common collocations: a different approach, approach a problem, practical approach.
Able to be used or obtained; not busy or occupied. "Fresh vegetables are available at the local market every morning." Common collocations: readily available, make available, available resources.
An advantage or profit gained from something. "Regular exercise has a clear benefit for both physical and mental health." Common collocations: benefit from, mutual benefit, health benefits.

A task or situation that tests someone's abilities; something difficult. "Learning a new language is a real challenge for most adults." Common collocations: face a challenge, major challenge, meet the challenge.

A group of people living in the same area or sharing common interests. "The local community organized a festival to celebrate their traditions." Common collocations: local community, community service, sense of community.

To think carefully about something before making a decision. "You should consider all the options before choosing a university." Common collocations: carefully consider, consider the possibility, widely considered.

To give something (money, time, ideas) to help achieve or provide something. "Volunteers contribute their time to help those in need." Common collocations: contribute to, contribute significantly, contribute ideas.
An insistent request or the desire of consumers for a product or service. "There is a growing demand for online education worldwide." Common collocations: meet the demand, high demand, demand for.
To grow or cause to grow and become more advanced or mature. "The city plans to develop new housing in the eastern district." Common collocations: develop skills, develop a plan, rapidly develop.

The surroundings or conditions in which a person lives or operates; the natural world. "Protecting the environment is one of the biggest issues of our time." Common collocations: natural environment, working environment, protect the environment.

To set up or create something on a firm or permanent basis. "The company was established in 1995 and has grown ever since." Common collocations: establish a business, well established, establish a connection.

Facts or information indicating whether a belief or claim is true. "There is strong evidence that smoking causes serious health problems." Common collocations: provide evidence, scientific evidence, evidence suggests.
A circumstance or element that contributes to a result. "Cost is an important factor when choosing where to study abroad." Common collocations: key factor, contributing factor, decisive factor.

All the people born and living around the same time; the production of something. "The younger generation is more familiar with digital technology." Common collocations: future generation, generation gap, power generation.
To recognize or establish what something or someone is. "Scientists were able to identify the cause of the disease." Common collocations: identify a problem, easily identify, identify with.
A strong effect or influence on someone or something. "Tourism has had a huge impact on the local economy." Common collocations: have an impact, significant impact, environmental impact.

To make or become better in quality, value, or condition. "Reading regularly can greatly improve your vocabulary and writing skills." Common collocations: improve performance, significantly improve, room for improvement.
To become or make greater in size, amount, or degree. "The population is expected to increase by 10% over the next decade." Common collocations: increase in, sharp increase, steadily increase.

A single person, considered separately from a group or society. "Every individual has the right to access quality education." Common collocations: individual needs, individual responsibility, each individual.

To include or contain as a necessary part; to cause someone to participate. "The project will involve working closely with local farmers." Common collocations: involve in, closely involved, actively involved.
An important topic or problem for discussion or debate. "Pollution is a serious issue in many large cities around the world." Common collocations: key issue, raise an issue, address an issue.

To keep something in its existing state or at the same level. "It is important to maintain a healthy diet and regular exercise routine." Common collocations: maintain standards, maintain a balance, maintain contact.
Easily seen, recognized, or understood; clear and evident. "It was obvious that he had not prepared for the presentation." Common collocations: fairly obvious, obvious reason, immediately obvious.

A time or situation that makes it possible to do something. "Studying abroad provides a great opportunity to experience different cultures." Common collocations: take the opportunity, job opportunity, equal opportunity.
To a higher degree than usual; especially. "The exam was particularly difficult this year compared to last year." Common collocations: particularly important, particularly useful, particularly in.

To stop something from happening or someone from doing something. "Washing your hands regularly can help prevent the spread of disease." Common collocations: prevent damage, prevent access, in order to prevent.

To make available for use; to supply or give something needed. "The government should provide affordable housing for low-income families." Common collocations: provide information, provide support, provide services.
To make smaller or less in amount, degree, or size. "The company plans to reduce costs by using less packaging material." Common collocations: reduce the risk, significantly reduce, reduce emissions.
To need something or make something necessary. "This course will require students to complete a research project." Common collocations: require attention, legally required, require effort.

A supply of something that a country, organization, or person has and can use. "Water is a valuable natural resource that must be protected." Common collocations: natural resources, human resources, limited resources.

Large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed. "There has been a significant improvement in air quality this year." Common collocations: significant change, significant difference, statistically significant.

A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation. "Education is often seen as the best solution to poverty." Common collocations: find a solution, possible solution, practical solution.

A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim. "The business developed a new strategy to attract younger customers." Common collocations: develop a strategy, marketing strategy, effective strategy.

Enough; adequate for a particular purpose. "Make sure you have sufficient time to complete the test before handing it in." Common collocations: sufficient evidence, sufficient funds, more than sufficient.

To give assistance, encouragement, or approval to someone or something. "The data strongly supports the conclusion that diet affects health." Common collocations: provide support, financial support, support a claim.

A general direction in which something is developing or changing. "There is a growing trend toward working from home in many industries." Common collocations: current trend, follow a trend, upward trend.
Suitable or proper in the circumstances. "It is important to wear appropriate clothing to a job interview." Common collocations: appropriate behavior, appropriate measures, entirely appropriate.

The power or right to give orders, make decisions, or enforce rules. "The local authority is responsible for maintaining public parks." Common collocations: local authority, authority over, in a position of authority.

To be composed or made up of particular elements or ingredients. "The exam consists of four sections: reading, writing, listening, and speaking." Common collocations: consist of, mainly consist, consist entirely.

To bring something into existence; to produce something new. "The aim of the project is to create more jobs for young people." Common collocations: create opportunities, create awareness, create a plan.

To plan and make something for a specific purpose; a plan or drawing. "Engineers designed the bridge to withstand extreme weather conditions." Common collocations: design a system, by design, product design.

The system of trade and industry by which the wealth of a country is managed. "Tourism plays a vital role in the country's economy." Common collocations: global economy, economy grows, boost the economy.
A distinctive attribute or characteristic of something. "The main feature of this phone is its long-lasting battery." Common collocations: key feature, main feature, special feature.

A particular way of doing something; a systematic procedure. "Scientists used a new method to test the quality of drinking water." Common collocations: teaching method, research method, effective method.
To happen or take place, especially unexpectedly. "Earthquakes occur frequently in that part of the world." Common collocations: commonly occur, likely to occur, occur naturally.

A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end. "The application process can take up to six weeks to complete." Common collocations: learning process, decision-making process, lengthy process.

To say or do something as a reaction to something that has been said or done. "The government was slow to respond to the growing housing crisis." Common collocations: respond to, respond quickly, respond positively.
